artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

Split Enz.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
I Got You" is not an album by Split Enz, but rather the title of their most successful single, released in January 1980 as the lead track from their fifth studio album, True Colours. The song exemplifies the band's blend of new wave, pop, and rock, marked by catchy melodies, layered harmonies, and a distinctive guitar riff played by Neil Finn. Its upbeat, synth-tinged sound helped define the early 1980s pop-rock landscape and showcased Split Enz’s transition toward a more accessible style, while still retaining their quirky, art-rock roots.

True Colours, released in 1980 on Mushroom Records in Australasia and A&M Records internationally, marked a turning point in Split Enz’s career, becoming their first major commercial breakthrough. The album features pronounced contributions from Neil Finn, whose songwriting—including "I Got You"—helped propel the band to international fame. Although the band and label initially doubted the hit potential of "I Got You," the song topped charts in Australia and New Zealand and reached the top 20 in the UK and top 10 in Canada. The album itself was widely praised for its inventive arrangements and genre-blending style, cementing Split Enz’s reputation as pioneers of New Zealand and Australian rock.
